newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says will not "import" labour rigidities.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says will not "import" labour rigidities.

text.p: A Labour government would not "import" labour market rigidities from other European Union states, a senior economics spokesman said on Monday.
The ruling Conservatives have accused Labour of planning to hamstring British industry by signing up to the EU Social Chapter, which is designed to set minimum working conditions.

But Shadow Chief Secretary to the Treasury Alastair Darling said such rigidities were generally the result of legislation in a particular country, rather than regulations of the EU as a whole. "They (other EU states) could get rid of them tomorrow if they wanted to. There is no question of us importing them here," he told the annual dinner of the City of London Corporation.
Darling said there had so far been only two measures produced under the Social Chapter -- one of paternity leave and the other on larger firms consulting their workers.
"There is nothing else. And as (shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer) Gordon Brown made clear last week, we will not accept measures that make our country less competitive," he added.
